problem: Current point goal navigation (PGN) models are learned by and tied to a single robot's platform (first-person view images, turn/forward actions), so they cannot be transferred to other robots, especially unknown or black-box ones.
motivation: Multi-robot systems need a way to transfer a teacher's PGN model to heterogeneous students. Local maps (SLAM/SfM) are a platform-independent modality that any robot can build and interpret, so a state-action map defined on local maps and grid subgoals could be universal.
key_idea: Distill a teacher RL PGN policy (NNQL on FPV images) into a student MLP that takes third-person-view BEV local maps and outputs grid subgoal actions, using rank-based KD and a rotation-invariant local map descriptor to cut the number of training episodes.
insight: The distilled student MLP matches or in one workspace beats the NNQL teacher (54.11 vs 50.82 in 00802), which the authors attribute to dimensionality reduction and representation learning during distillation. The evidence is thin: there are no ablations, only three workspaces and one table, and no comparison against other PGN or KD methods.
method: Teacher PGN: Nearest-Neighbor Q-learning (NNQL) on RRE embeddings, with alpha=0.1 and gamma=0.9. The reward is the change in Dijkstra shortest-path cost from an oracle obstacle map.
Embedding model: a VGG16 place classifier over 600 place classes (10x5 grid x 12 angles) whose class-probability map is converted into a reciprocal rank embedding (RRE) vector.

Student model: an MLP with hidden layers of 2048 and 1024 units, ReLU, and a 13-way softmax over turn actions (turn theta in {theta_o, 0, ±30..180} then 0.5 m forward). Its input is the RRE embedding of the BEV local map (2.5 m radius, omnidirectional).
Cross-architecture KD: the teacher's class-specific L1-normalized reciprocal-rank vectors replace probability vectors in Hinton-style KD, with a KL loss, Adam (lr 0.001) and batch size 32.

Invariant reference coordinate: the local map is rotated into a rotation-invariant frame by hue-histogram entropy minimization. Place classes shrink from 600 to 50 (j=i/12), so multiple episodes collapse into one and the KD loss is computed in 50 dimensions.
Bumper: a collision-avoidance mechanism removes unsafe action candidates, so the planner scores only the safe ones.

setting.backbone: NNQL teacher (VGG16 place classifier + RRE embedding) distilled into an MLP student (2048-1024-13)
setting.training_data: Teacher episodes collected by epsilon-greedy Q-learning in three Habitat-Sim scenes (max 4 steps per episode); no external data
setting.observation: Teacher: FPV RGB images. Student: BEV omnidirectional local map (2.5 m radius) reconstructed via SLAM/SfM
setting.action_space: 13 discrete turn angles followed by a 0.5 m forward move (subgoals on a regular grid)
setting.privileged: Oracle BEV obstacle grid map (0.1 m) with Dijkstra for rewards/annotation during training only; bumper at test time

numbers_note: The custom goal achievement rates (00800: NNQL 44.21, MLP 42.03; 00801: NNQL 29.20, MLP 27.12; 00802: NNQL 50.82, MLP 54.11) come from three Habitat-Sim scenes with a 0.25 m radius and 50-step budget. They match no canonical benchmark, so they are omitted here.
results: Across three Habitat scenes the distilled MLP student reaches 42.03/27.12/54.11% goal achievement, close to the NNQL teacher (44.21/29.20/50.82%) and well above a random planner (10.20/8.10/12.60%). It beats the teacher only in 00802.
limitations: Tiny proof-of-concept: three scenes, one table, no ablations of the LMD/entropy alignment, and no comparison with other PGN or KD methods

Simplistic assumptions: the local map is an idealized 2D BEV circle rather than a real SLAM output, the oracle map is required in training, a bumper is assumed, and the student is not tested on genuinely different robot platforms
Success rates are low (about 27–54%) and no standard metrics (SPL, SR on standard PGN benchmarks) are reported
